 OKLAHOMA CITY (KOKH) — A state agency is expanding a recall of medical marijuana in Oklahoma that failed required testing.
 Earlier this month, the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority issued a recall for two medical marijuana flower production batches from Blue Collar Criminals Collective.
 OMMA received a self-report from the grow facility to report that specific flower production batches had failed required testing after being sent to dispensaries.
 OMMA says the batches failed testing for yeast and mold.
 "OMMA extends a huge shoutout to Blue Collar Criminals Collective, LLC for their quick self-reporting and commitment to safety. Their diligence and fast action helped stop the spread of potentially unsafe products and set a great example of accountability and transparency in Oklahoma's medical marijuana industry," a statement from OMMA read. 
 Following the announcement of the recall, OMMA received questions regarding products from batch number BIS091326-2. 
 Officials say that while the batch initially passed lab testing, a portion of it was later mixed with a failed batch, making those specific mixed products unsafe. 
 On Monday, OMMA expanded the recall to include only mixed products from batch BIS091326-2. 
 To see a complete list of the batches affected, visit OMMA's website here. 
 Patients who purchased the recalled items should dispose of the products or contact the dispensary where they were purchased.
 Dispensaries are also being told to remove the recalled products from shelves immediately.
